tasks.do: Define a cross-cutting concern and give three real examples.
Define aspect, join point, pointcut, advice, advisor, target, proxy, and weaving — precisely.
State what a join point can be in Spring AOP, and what it can additionally be in AspectJ.
Explain when weaving happens in Spring AOP versus AspectJ.
Name the `BeanPostProcessor` that creates AOP proxies.
Explain the relationship between Spring AOP and AspectJ annotations.
List the situations that require real AspectJ weaving instead.
Enable AOP in plain Spring and describe what Spring Boot does automatically.
Map every vocabulary term onto a concrete piece of a working aspect.
In Spring AOP, a join point is ALWAYS a method execution.
Pointcut selects; advice acts. Do not swap them.
Spring weaves at runtime by creating proxies, not at compile time.
`@Aspect` alone does nothing — the class must also be a Spring bean.
An advisor is pointcut + advice, not a synonym for aspect.
`private`, `final`, and self-invoked methods are unadvisable — a proxy limitation.
